scenes.title: Lift the Handle
scenes.summary: F1 arrives for her first morning shift and M1 shows her the trick to the front door and his paper ledger.
scenes.intro: {F1} arrives early for her very first morning at the {SHOW} guesthouse in {CITY}. Behind the front desk, veteran handyman {M1} is already pouring strong tea. Listen to the scene first without worrying about catching every word.
story: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?
Good morning. No, lift the handle first, then push.
Oh, it opens! Thank you. I am {F1}, the new receptionist.
I am {M1}. You are ten minutes early.
I always walk fast on my first day. Where is the computer?
In the drawer. Here we use this big paper book and a pencil.
Paper still works when the power goes out.
Fair enough! And these are the keys?
Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.
Great. Tell me everything I need to know.
Rule one: drink hot tea first, then answer the bell.
scenes.outro: {F1} is inside, the eight brass keys are on the board, and her first morning has begun. Don't worry if a few words went past quickly; they come back all week. See you next time.

scenes.title: Warm Rolls and Two Rings
scenes.summary: Morning baker F2 welcomes F1 with fresh bread and warns her about Room 4's double buzzer.
scenes.intro: Five minutes later, a warm smell of fresh bread fills the lobby from the small breakfast corner. {F2} carries out a basket of hot rolls to meet {F1} and {M1}. Let's listen in first.
story: Hello! You must be {F1}. I am {F2} from the kitchen.
Nice to meet you, {F2}. Something smells wonderful!
Fresh morning rolls! Take one while it is still warm.
Thank you! Do we use first names here?
With me, always! Leave the stiff polite talk for the guests.
{F2} talks to everyone on our street like old friends.
Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!
What was that bell? Somebody rang twice!
Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.
Even when room four is empty, the old wire rings twice.
So the house says hello on its own?
Exactly! You already fit right in.
scenes.outro: {F1} has a warm roll in her hand and a friendly ally in the café corner. You will hear those casual and polite greetings side by side in every episode. See you next time.

scenes.title: Where Are My Glasses?
scenes.summary: Anxious owner M2 rushes in worried about today's Room 4 arrival while hunting for the glasses on his forehead.
scenes.intro: Before the first guest arrives, guesthouse owner {M2} hurries in from the courtyard looking flustered. {F1} and {M1} watch as {M2} searches his pockets in a panic. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, {F1}. Is everything ready?
Good morning! Yes, the desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Today's guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!
Relax, {M2}. The room is clean and the towels are fresh.
I need to read the reservation book, but I cannot find my glasses!
Are they in your coat pocket?
No, only my pen and three old receipts!
Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss.
Why would my glasses be in the... oh! They are on my head!
Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.
Do not tell anyone! Now, smile brightly when the bell rings.
Here comes a taxi at the gate right now.
scenes.outro: {M2} found his glasses on his own forehead just as the taxi pulled up outside. Relax and let the rhythm of the words sink in; see you next time.

scenes.title: Room Four on the Second Floor
scenes.summary: Retired music teacher F3 checks into Room 4 with a heavy blue suitcase after a long train ride.
scenes.intro: At the front desk, retired music teacher {F3} steps inside from her taxi pulling a large dark-blue suitcase. {F1} greets her first real guest while {M1} stands ready to help with the bag. Let's hear how it goes.
story: Good morning, my dear. I have a booking for {F3}.
Yes, room four on the second floor! How was your train trip?
Quiet and pleasant, thank you, though this suitcase feels very heavy today.
Allow me. Goodness, did you pack stones in here?
Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!
Here is your key, number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.
Wonderful. Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
The courtyard, right above the old tree. It is very quiet.
Just what I need. Where are the stairs?
Right through this archway. I will carry the blue bag up for you.
scenes.outro: {F1} handled her first check-in smoothly, though {M1} noticed that blue suitcase felt strangely heavy. See you next time to find out why.

scenes.title: Not My Clothes!
scenes.summary: Upstairs in Room 4, F3 opens the blue suitcase and discovers men's shoes and a wooden toy train instead of her clothes.
scenes.intro: Two minutes after going upstairs, Room 4's buzzer rings at the desk—not twice, but four times in a row. {F1} hurries up to find {F3} and {M1} staring at the open suitcase on the stand. Listen first.
story: Madam {F3}, is everything alright? You rang the bell!
Look inside this suitcase, {F1}! This is not my bag!
Wait—it is dark blue, just like yours!
The outside is identical, yes! But look inside!
Two pairs of big brown men's shoes and grey sweaters.
And what is this wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!
I certainly do not wear size forty-four shoes!
No wonder it was so heavy. Wood and leather!
Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!
Please sit down, madam. Do not worry, we will check the tag right now.
There is a small paper card tied to the side handle.
Oh, let us bring it downstairs to the light!
scenes.outro: Instead of dresses and sheet music, the blue suitcase holds big brown shoes and a wooden toy train. Let's see what is written on that tag next time.

scenes.title: The Luggage Tag
scenes.summary: At the front desk, M2 reads the tiny handwriting on the suitcase tag while F1 calls the station office.
scenes.intro: Back at the front desk, {F1}, {F3}, and owner {M2} lean over the blue suitcase under the desk lamp. {M2} finally puts his glasses to good use. Listen to the scene first.
story: Dear me, what a mix-up! Let me look at the tag with my glasses.
Is there a name or a phone number on it?
No phone number, unfortunately. Only two initials and an old street name.
Wait—that street is right here in our neighbourhood, five minutes away!
How strange! We rode the same morning train to the same district.
{F1}, call the station lost-and-found office right away.
I am dialling now... Hello? Did anyone report a swapped blue suitcase?
Tell them mine has a red ribbon inside the top pocket!
Not yet? Please take our guesthouse number and address. Thank you!
They have nothing yet, madam, I am terribly sorry.
It is not your fault. Still, I only have the coat on my back!
Wait one moment—{F2} in the café just waved to me with an idea!
scenes.outro: No luck at the train station yet, and the mysterious owner lives just five minutes away. Next time, {F2} steps in to rescue {F3}'s evening.

scenes.title: Tea and a Warm Cardigan
scenes.summary: F2 lends F3 a clean soft cardigan and pours herbal tea while M1 locks the mystery suitcase safely away.
scenes.intro: In the cosy café corner, {F2} brings over a pot of hot tea and a neatly folded cream cardigan for {F3}, while {M1} carries the mystery suitcase to the closet behind the desk. Listen first.
story: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea and honey.
Oh, thank you, {F2}. My hands were cold from the shock!
And look—this soft wool cardigan is clean and never worn. Try it on.
Are you sure? It looks lovely and warm!
It fits you very well, madam.
You good people are saving my whole trip.
A traveller cannot sit upstairs sad on her first evening in {CITY}!
I locked the other blue suitcase safely in our luggage closet.
Thank you, {M1}. That little wooden train inside looked old and precious.
Whoever owns it will surely look for it soon.
I think I will sleep well tonight after all.
Rest well, madam. Ring down if you need anything.
scenes.outro: Warm mint tea and a borrowed cardigan turned a bad afternoon into a gentle evening. One more scene remains in Episode 1—and a surprise is waiting at the door. See you next time.

scenes.title: Left on the Step
scenes.summary: Late at night the front bell rings, and F1 and M1 find F3's real suitcase on the step with an anonymous note.
scenes.intro: It is almost nine in the evening, and the courtyard lamps are glowing softly as {F1} finishes her first day with {M1}. Suddenly, the front gate bell rings once in the quiet night. Listen first.
story: Did you hear that, {M1}? Someone just rang the gate bell!
At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.
Hello? Good evening! Nobody is standing at the gate!
Wait. Look down on the stone step.
Another dark-blue suitcase! Is this Madam {F3}'s bag?
Check the zipper... yes, her initials are right here!
Why did the person run away without taking his own suitcase back?
Look, there is a folded white envelope taped to the handle.
Let me read it: 'Sorry for the mistake. Please keep my blue bag until Friday.'
Until Friday? No name, no signature!
Why leave your own shoes and wooden train with strangers until Friday?
Welcome to the {SHOW}, {F1}. Your second day will not be boring.
scenes.outro: Madam {F3}'s suitcase is back, yet the mystery stranger vanished into the night and asked them to guard his bag until Friday. Episode 1 is complete—see you next time for Episode 2!
